rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3.3, 6.2.4, 6.2.6, 7 and Tables 10-12 report the authors' own on-farm data from 71 farmers' fields in western Uttar Pradesh (water productivity, yield, earthwork cost) and a PRA survey in 10 villages, alongside reviewed material.
rows.notes: The document is a technical bulletin on laser land leveling for rice-wheat systems in the Indo-Gangetic Plains; it contains no drip or subsurface drip irrigation experiment. Its own results concern water saving, water productivity and yield under laser-leveled versus traditionally leveled surface-irrigated fields, not SSDI under conservation agriculture. Q1 is borderline because much of the bulletin is descriptive/review; counted yes only because of the original 71-field dataset and PRA survey.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3.3, 6.2.4, 6.2.6, 7 and Tables 10-12 report own on-farm data from 71 farmers' fields and a PRA survey in 10 villages.
rows.notes: No evidence on drip/SSDI at all; the technology studied is laser land leveling. The bulletin does report reduced coefficient of variation in yield and water productivity across farmers under laser leveling (Tables 10, 11), which could be read as a stability/risk outcome, but for a different technology than the passage names. Technology mismatch.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through annexure and glossary). The study is cited by the review for an SSDI-plus-CA claim, but it is entirely about laser land leveling in surface-irrigated rice-wheat systems; the water-saving figures in the review's context (46.7%, 44.7%) do not appear in this document.
